sub_answers.sub_question: What documented financial difficulties, sponsorship withdrawals, or insolvency events has the club experienced and when?
sub_answers.text: CFR Cluj entered insolvency after the 2014–15 season leading to serious financial difficulties and a 24-point deduction by the Romanian Football Federation for failing to fully remunerate five former players, an action later overturned by the Court of Arbitration for Sport in May 2015 [d2376249s5p0]. Kagua-Erave FC received reported financial backing of K 60,000 from two backers ahead of the 2019 season and in early May 2019 their participation in the playoffs was thrown into doubt after reports that players had not been paid [d60559687s1p0][d60559687s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What disputes, sanctions, or controversies involving club officials, players, or administrators have been publicly reported?
sub_answers.text: CFR Cluj's owner Pászkány faced legal charges and was reported to have neglected the team during the 2012–2017 decline period [d2376249s5p0]. The Romanian Football Federation deducted 24 points from CFR for unpaid former players, a sanction the club later successfully appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport [d2376249s5p0]. Kagua-Erave FC had a reported dispute related to unpaid players in early May 2019 which cast doubt over their playoff participation [d60559687s1p0].

sub_answers.text: CFR Cluj contested a 24-point deduction by the Romanian Football Federation over unpaid wages and successfully appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport in May 2015, which restored the deducted points [d2376249s5p0]. Dinamo București's filing for insolvency rendered them ineligible for European competitions, which indirectly affected CFR's European qualification for 2013–14 [d2376249s5p0]. Kagua-Erave FC's playoff participation was jeopardised in May 2019 due to reports of unpaid players but the club ultimately took the field in the quarter-finals [d60559687s1p0].

sub_answers.text: Danone ended its sponsorship after the 2013–14 Ligue 1 season, leaving the club without its long-time sponsor [d5697687s8p0]. The club was relegated at the end of the 2014–15 Ligue 1 season amid worsening finances [d5697687s8p0]. Evian were relegated again after the 2015–16 Ligue 2 season as financial problems continued [d5697687s8p0]. The club was placed in receivership on 2 August 2016 and given a two-month probationary period to resolve its finances [d5697687s8p0]. On 9 August 2016 the French Football Federation confirmed Evian's decision to cease operation in the CFA and the club shuttered shortly afterwards [d5697687s8p0].

sub_answers.text: The DNCG imposed an additional administrative relegation on the club due to its deteriorating finances, which would have placed Evian in the fourth tier (CFA) [d5697687s8p0]. The club was placed in receivership on 2 August 2016 and given a two-month probationary period to save itself, tied to its ability to meet regulatory/financial requirements [d5697687s8p0]. The French Football Federation confirmed the club's decision to cease operation in the CFA on 9 August 2016 after the club failed to resolve its financial difficulties [d5697687s8p0].

sub_answers.text: The club was taken over by DFC 1883 Ltd, which immediately formed a new club after the old company was wound up and the FA expelled the previous club from the FA register [d451159s4p0]. In February 2013 the Darlington Football Club Community Interest Company (DFC CIC) acquired a 52% stake, the Supporters' Club held 15% and individual fans held 33%, giving 100% fan- and community-ownership [d451159s4p0]. An appeal against treating the new club as a distinct entity (and preventing it from playing under the name Darlington F.C.) was rejected by the FA, which effected the change of registration and name control [d451159s4p0].

sub_answers.text: The Football Association placed the new club in the Northern League Division One because the proposed playing ground lacked the grading required for the Northern Premier League, and that placement determined the club's initial step in the pyramid [d451159s4p0]. On the field, promotion outcomes recorded were: champions of Northern League Division One (2012–13) which earned promotion, and subsequent playoff results (runners-up and playoff final wins) that produced further promotions in following seasons [d451159s4p0]. Ground-grading issues were applied to prevent the club participating in a higher-level play-off despite finishing in play-off positions, thereby influencing placement independent of on-pitch results [d451159s4p0].
